summary.name: Audacity
summary.one_liner: Audacity is a free, open-source audio editor and recorder for multi-track recording, editing, mixing and audio format conversion.
use_cases: Converting audio files between WAV, MP3, FLAC and Ogg
Analyzing audio frequencies with a spectrogram
Adding third-party VST3 or Nyquist plugins to audio projects
summary.what_it_does: Audacity records and edits audio, supporting multi-track work for music, podcasts and general sound editing. It imports, exports and converts all major audio formats, including WAV to MP3, FLAC and Ogg. It supports third-party plugins such as VST3 and Nyquist. Its Spectrogram view and Vamp analyzers allow frequency visualization and deeper audio analysis. The page also mentions Audio.com as an online companion for collaboration, versioned backups and sharing.
notable: Free and open source, with source code open to view and modify
Official distributor MuseHub bundles free extras such as Muse Sounds, Elements and Muse FX
Spectrogram view and Vamp scientific analyzers for frequency analysis
Audacity 4 adds updated UI and Workspaces; OpenVINO AI plugins announced for macOS
caveats: Several MuseHub add-ons (such as Soap, Trinity EQ, Graillon 3) are listed as separate products and may be paid; the page does not state their prices
Audacity 3.7 is noted as 'Under Maintenance' on the page
AI features such as music separation and noise suppression are described as coming to macOS, not yet confirmed as available
